title: Reward biases spontaneous neural reactivation during sleep

funding_references.award_title: National Center of Competence in Research (NCCR) Affective Sciences

description: Simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset from 18 participants who played two games (a face game and a maze game) during wakefulness in a 3T MRI scanner. One game was randomly assigned to be won (reward) and the other lost (no reward). Participants then slept in the scanner with 64-channel EEG for 1-2 hours. A classifier trained on game-session data was applied to sleep-session fMRI to examine reward-biased spontaneous neural reactivation, and memory for both tasks was tested the next day.
methods_description: Participants performed the FACE and MAZE games interleaved with rest and preparation periods during fMRI at 3T. After the game session, 64 EEG electrodes were placed and participants slept in the MRI for 1-2 hours with simultaneous EEG. A decoding classifier trained on wake game-session data was applied to sleep-session fMRI data. A memory test on both tasks was done the next day. The dataset includes task EPI sessions, a resting/sleep EPI session, an EEG file for the sleep session, and a T1 anatomical image.
